Hi Irene / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security and legal teams as we work through the SIG/CAIQ:

1) Tenant-specific retention: Our forensics team needs a short-term extension for tenant "medivar-prod" logs (auth + audit + request tracing) to 120 days instead of your default 30 days while we complete an internal product migration. Is a tenant-scoped retention carve-out possible for a hosted account, or is that limited to Dedicated/Private deployments?

2) Preservation & proof of deletion: For SOC2 evidence, we need a sample of the deletion proof artifact that Redwood would provide when TTL expires (proof of erase / delete audit entry + hash or snapshot id). Can you share the deletion playbook or a representative deletion log?

3) SAR export path: If we request a full-account export for an SAR, what are the supported delivery options (S3 bucket, secure FTP, Drive)? We need to confirm encryption-in-flight and at-rest and whether you can write to a customer-owned S3 bucket in the same AWS account.

We've attached the SIG questionnaire with the specific questions highlighted (MediVar_SIG_questionnaire_v2.xlsx).

Helpful context: this is for a prospective contract; timeline is tight (we'd like artifacts in ~7 business days). Please call out anything that requires legal/procurement sign-off.

Best,
Linda Park
Director, Information Security
MediVar Health

Subject: Re: Retention bridging for MediVar - SIG/CAIQ follow-up

Hi Linda — appreciate the clear ask and the deadline. Short answers up front, then a proposed next step.

1) Tenant-specific retention: For Hosted API customers we support targeted retention carve-outs via an exceptions process — we can retain specific telemetry/log streams for a tenant for up to 180 days, but it requires: (a) formal exception ticket, (b) signed data handling addendum, and (c) scoped access controls. Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention at the pool level without the same exception flow.

2) Proof of deletion: We can produce a deletion artifact that includes: retention policy id, object ids removed, UTC timestamps, and a deletion checksum (SHA256) bound to the deletion job id. We have a sample deletion audit entry and a short deletion playbook; attached is a draft tech note that outlines the artifact and the limitations around ephemeral KV cache entries (those are wiped on node restart and do not have stable object ids).

3) SAR export: We support customer-owned S3 buckets (we will assume an IAM write role you provide), and transfers are performed over TLS 1.2+. Exports are encrypted at-rest with AES-256 using customer-managed keys where available. We can also deliver to a secure SFTP endpoint but Google Drive is only available as an ad-hoc share for small exports.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: produce the retention matrix + deletion playbook we will share with MediVar.
- Jonas: draft the forensics snapshot procedure and the sample deletion log exports.
- Ben: start the exception request paperwork and loop in procurement if needed.

If that works I can pull the artifacts together into a single evidence pack (redaction-friendly) and send over a secure Drive link. We can also set up a 30-minute runbook review with your SOC team the week of Sep 7.

I'll attach the draft tech note for now so your engineers can review the details.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that's helpful. A few clarifying points from our side so your team can scope the artifacts:

- For the deletion artifact we specifically need an example that shows the full lifecycle for a log object: ingestion --> retention decision --> deletion job id/timestamp --> final delete confirmation. A redacted sample is fine.
- For SAR exports: customer-owned S3 is preferred. Please call out the exact permissions your role will need to write to our bucket.
- HIPAA note: our compliance team requests that retention carve-outs explicitly reference whether pseudonymized PHI can be retained and what redaction capabilities exist at export time.

If you can give us those three items (sample deletion artifact, retention matrix, SAR S3 write pattern) in the next 5 business days we'll be able to proceed with legal review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — feel free to send the Drive link privately.

Linda
